title: Lightmass & Quality Settings 🎛️
description: Tweak Lightmass for optimal bake times and visual fidelity.

slides.title: Lightmass Settings ⚙️
slides.content:
# Control the Bake

In **World Settings** (Window → World Settings), find the **Lightmass** section. These settings affect all static/stationary lights in the level.

* **Static Lighting Level Scale** – smaller = finer detail but longer bake. Default 1.0. For small archviz, try 0.1.
* **Num Indirect Lighting Bounces** – how many times light bounces. More = brighter, softer GI. 10 for production, 3 for preview.
* **Indirect Lighting Quality** – higher = smoother results, slower.
* **Indirect Lighting Smoothness** – reduces lightmap noise.

Start with preview settings (low quality) for fast iteration, then crank up for final bake.

quizData.question: Which setting controls how many times light bounces for GI?
quizData.explanation: Num Indirect Lighting Bounces determines how far light propagates indirectly. Higher = more realistic GI.

slides.title: Lightmap Density 🗺️
slides.content:
## Per‑Mesh Quality

Each static mesh has a **Lightmap Resolution** property (under Static Mesh Settings). Higher resolution = more detail but more memory.

* Use the **Lightmap Density** view mode (Alt+6) to see a heatmap.
* Green = optimal, Red = too high, Blue = too low.
* Adjust resolution per mesh in the Details panel.

The Lightmap Resolution scales with the mesh size; larger meshes need higher absolute resolution.

slides.title: Build Times & Swarm 🐝
slides.content:
## Speed Up Baking

Lightmass uses **Swarm** to distribute baking across multiple machines on a network (advanced). But locally, you can:

* Reduce **Static Lighting Level Scale** slightly.
* Limit **Num Indirect Lighting Bounces** for test bakes.
* Use **Lightmass Importance Volume** to focus computation only where needed (place a volume around playable area).

Always place an **Importance Volume** to avoid wasting bake time on far‑off areas.

quizData.question: The view mode that shows lightmap density is accessed by pressing _____+6.
quizData.explanation: Alt+6 shows the Lightmap Density view mode, colour‑coding meshes by their lightmap texel density.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Lightmass Portals

For interiors, place **Lightmass Portals** in windows. They tell Lightmass where light enters, greatly improving indoor GI quality.
